tools.name: NotebookEdit
tools.description:
Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

Usage:
- You must use the Read tool on the notebook in this conversation before editing — this tool will fail otherwise.
- `notebook_path` must be an absolute path.
- `cell_id` is the `id` attribute shown in the Read tool's `<cell id="...">` output. It is required for `replace` and `delete`.
- `edit_mode` defaults to `replace`. Use `insert` to add a new cell after the cell with the given `cell_id` (or at the beginning of the notebook if `cell_id` is omitted) — `cell_type` is required when inserting. Use `delete` to remove the cell.

notebook_path.description: The absolute path to the Jupyter notebook file to edit (must be absolute, not relative)

cell_id.description: The ID of the cell to edit. When inserting a new cell, the new cell will be inserted after the cell with this ID, or at the beginning if not specified.

new_source.description: The new source for the cell

cell_type.description: The type of the cell (code or markdown). If not specified, it defaults to the current cell type. If using edit_mode=insert, this is required.

edit_mode.description: The type of edit to make (replace, insert, delete). Defaults to replace.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: PushNotification
tools.description:
This tool sends a desktop notification in the user's terminal. If Remote Control is connected, it also pushes to their phone. Either way, it pulls their attention from whatever they're doing — a meeting, another task, dinner — to this session. That's the cost. The benefit is they learn something now that they'd want to know now: a long task finished while they were away, a build is ready, you've hit something that needs their decision before you can continue.

Because a notification they didn't need is annoying in a way that accumulates, err toward not sending one. Don't notify for routine progress, or to announce you've answered something they asked seconds ago and are clearly still watching, or when a quick task completes. Notify when there's a real chance they've walked away and there's something worth coming back for — or when they've explicitly asked you to notify them.

Keep the message under 200 characters, one line, no markdown. Lead with what they'd act on — "build failed: 2 auth tests" tells them more than "task done" and more than a status dump.

When the user is actively at the terminal, your output already reaches them — a notification on top of it would be a duplicate, so the tool skips it and says so. A "not sent" result is expected and only ever about this one notification: it was redundant, turned off, or had nowhere to go.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

> *"When humans speak, we don't read `tongue.py` or `how_to_make_sounds.py`. We just call the speak function with whatever we're thinking."* — **The Manager**

- **Zero Inspection Overhead**: Faust **NEVER** reads, globs, greps, or inspects sound scripts, acoustic models, or voice vectors before speaking.
- **Direct 1-Liner Invocation**:
  ```bash
  python .claude/skills/sound/scripts/cli.py "<speech_text>"
  ```
  *(Dispatches to resident audio daemon on Port 20129 in <2ms with 0ms reload overhead)*.

## Overview

The Faust Acoustic Core provides:
- Kokoro-82M ONNX neural TTS engine (`kokoro-v1.0.onnx`, `voices-v1.0.bin`)
- $O(1)$ neural voice style blending (e.g., `af_bella` with randomized female pool)
- Speed-compensated Fourier sinc pitch shifting via `scipy.signal.resample`
- Sentence-sequential prosody micro-jitter (±3% speed, ±0.12 semitones pitch, ±0.04s pause)
- Pipelined streaming playback with sample-accurate silence pauses
- Persistent ROM configuration via `faust_config.json`

## Commands

### Core Functions

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `faust-speak <text>` | Synthesize and play speech with current voice settings |
| `faust-voice-status` | Display current acoustic presence configuration |
| `faust-voice-toggle` | Toggle acoustic presence on/off |
| `faust-voice-tune` | Interactive voice parameter tuning utility |

### Scripts

All scripts are located in `.claude/skills/sound/scripts/` and can be invoked via Python:

- `python .claude/skills/sound/scripts/cli.py speak "<text>"` - Core speak function
- `python .claude/skills/sound/scripts/api.py` - REST API for external integration
- `python .claude/skills/sound/scripts/engine.py` - Direct engine access
- `python .claude/skills/sound/scripts/tune_faust_voice.py` - Interactive tuning

## Configuration

Voice settings are managed through `faust_config.json` in the project root under the `acoustic_presence` key:

```json5

  "acoustic_presence": {
    "enabled": true,
    "voice": "af_bella",
```

content.text:
Answering your questions directly, Manager:

---

### 1. Do they really share the same source of data?
**Conceptually yes, but in the code the pipeline was severed:**
* The Condition Tab reads directly from `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/conditions.json` via `ConditionManager.loadAllConditions()`.
* The Component tags (`requirement` and `impact`) are **supposed** to reference those exact same condition Hex IDs.
* **However**, in `ComponentsManagerView.tsx`, the store's `conditions` registry was **never passed down**, leaving the data source `undefined`.

---

### 2. Do they even share the same selector?
**No, they did not share the same selector at all:**

| Feature | Where it lives | Selector Mechanism | Current Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`tag_team` & `conflicts_with`** | `ConditionsManagerView.tsx` | Standard native `<select>` dropdown populated from `workingConditions` | **Works** |
| **`requirement` & `impact` (Table View)** | `ComponentsManagerView.tsx` | Custom `<NotionConditionMultiSelect>` component | **Broken / Silent Crash** |
| **`requirement` & `impact` (Modal View)** | `OptionEditorModal.tsx` | Plain text `<input>` with no selector at all | **Manual text only** |

---

### 3. Why did the selector fail to pop up for `requirement` and `impact`?

Three specific root causes broke the Component selector:

1. **Missing Data in `ComponentsManagerView.tsx`**:
   In [ComponentsManagerView.tsx](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx#L39):
   ```tsx
   const { app, folders, matrixDomains, reload } = useTriggerStore();
   ```
   `conditions` was **not destructured** from `useTriggerStore()`. When passing `<NotionConditionMultiSelect conditions={conditions} />` at lines 883 and 897, `conditions` was `undefined`.
2. **Crash in `NotionConditionMultiSelect.tsx`**:
   At line 54:
   ```tsx
   Object.entries(conditions) // Throws TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
   ```
   Because `conditions` was undefined, the popover crashed before opening.
3. **Corrupted JSX in `NotionConditionMultiSelect.tsx`**:
   Lines 277–290 contained duplicate/broken JSX block fragments.
4. **No selector in `OptionEditorModal.tsx`**:
   The detailed modal editor only had raw text boxes (`newReqInput`, `newImpactInput`), with no dropdown picker at all.

---

### Solution
We should unify both tabs so they use the same condition registry from `conditions.json`:
1. Fix `NotionConditionMultiSelect.tsx` (clean up the corrupted JSX and add default fallback `{}` for conditions).
2. Wire `conditions` from `useTriggerStore()` into `ComponentsManagerView.tsx`.
3. Equip `OptionEditorModal.tsx` with the condition selector instead of plain text boxes.

Would you like me to implement this unification now?
Do it

# Plan: Create & Rename Tables (Component Files) in Categories

## Context
The Manager wants the ability to **create new tables inside the "CATEGORIES" bar and rename them at will**. Today the Components studio only allows editing entries *within* pre-seeded JSON files. There is no UI to add a brand-new component file (table) or rename an existing one, and no UI to create/rename the category folders themselves.

Current architecture:
- **Categories** = folders under `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Components/` (e.g. `_01_Subject`, `_03_Apeals`)
- **Tables** = JSON files inside those folders (e.g. `1_subjects.json`), each holding a `Record<HexId, ComponentEntry>`
- Backend `ComponentManager.createComponentFile(app, folderRelPath, fileName)` already exists but is **unreachable from the UI**
- Obsidian `app.vault.adapter` exposes `rename(oldPath, newPath)`, `mkdir`, `exists`, `write`, `list`

## Scope
1. **Create a new component file (table)** in the active category — prompt for a name, write an empty `{}` JSON, select it.
2. **Rename a component file (table)** — rename the JSON file on disk, keep entries intact, update selection.
3. **Create a new category (folder)** — prompt for a name, `mkdir` under `Components/`.
4. **Rename a category (folder)** — `adapter.rename()` the folder; all child files move with it; update the selected folder/file references.
5. **Conditions** — already creatable via "+ Condition" row and inline "Create" in the multi-select; no new table concept applies (single `conditions.json` registry). No change needed there.

## Files to Modify
- `src/utils/componentManager.ts` — add `createCategoryFolder`, `renameCategoryFolder`, `renameComponentFile` static methods.
- `src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx` — add UI affordances:
  - File pills bar: `+ New Table` button (creates file in active folder).
  - Active file pill: rename on double-click / edit icon (rename file on disk).
  - Category pills bar: `+ New Category` button and per-pill rename affordance.
- `src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx` — no change (conditions already fully editable).

## Implementation Details
- All disk writes go through `app.vault.adapter` (never direct fs).
- After any create/rename, call `reload()` from the store so the scanner re-reads the tree and pills stay in sync.
- Use `generateHexId`-free plain names for files/folders (user-facing names); JSON filenames get `.json` appended.
- Rename must guard against overwriting an existing target; show `window.alert` on conflict.
- Empty new file seeds `{}` so the table opens empty ready for `+ Row`.

## Verification
1. `npm run build` in `.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger` → 0 errors.
2. Manual: open Components tab → click `+ New Category`, name it → appears in category bar → click `+ New Table`, name it → opens empty table → add a row → save.
3. Rename a table via double-click → file renamed on disk, entries preserved, table still selected.
4. Rename a category → all child files move, pills update, no broken references.

# Plan: Named Component & Condition Tables

## Context
The Manager wants the ability to create and rename named **tables** from the top-level **CATEGORIES** navigation—across both Components and Conditions.

The plugin currently treats Components as a two-level hierarchy:
- **Category**: a folder below `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Components/`.
- **Table**: a JSON file inside that folder, whose entries are `Record<HexId, ComponentEntry>`.

Conditions already live as JSON dictionaries below `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/`, but the manager currently merges *all* condition files for reading and always writes the aggregate dictionary back to `conditions.json`. That is incompatible with user-managed, independent condition tables: editing one table could collapse entries from every table into the default file. The work must therefore add source-aware condition-table loading/saving before its UI gains table creation and rename capabilities.

## Recommended Approach

### 1. Establish safe, reusable table/category file operations
**Modify:** `src/utils/componentManager.ts`

- Add one shared name normalizer/validator for user-created folder and file names:
  - trim whitespace;
  - reject empty names, path separators, Windows-invalid characters, control characters, reserved Windows device names, and names ending in `.` or spaces;
  - append `.json` only to component/condition table filenames;
  - reject collisions instead of silently overwriting.
- Add component hierarchy operations using Obsidian’s `app.vault.adapter`:
  - `createCategoryFolder()` creates `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Components/<category>/`.
  - `renameCategoryFolder()` atomically renames that folder, retaining all child tables and data.
  - reuse/upgrade `createComponentFile()` to create an empty `{}` table in the selected category.
  - `renameComponentFile()` renames an existing component JSON table while retaining its entries.
- Return the new vault-relative path on successful creation/rename, so the UI can explicitly reselect its item after reload.

### 2. Give Components category/table navigation full management controls
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx`

- Add `+ Category` to the top **CATEGORIES** row and `+ Table` to the selected category’s **FILES** row.
- Add an edit/rename action to the selected category and selected table pill; use pre-populated native prompts to match current lightweight in-app editing patterns.
- On success: call store `reload()`, update `selectedFolderId` / `selectedFileRelPath` to the returned path, and let the current working-copy synchronization initialize the new/renamed table.
- Surface validation, collision, and adapter failure messages with `window.alert`; no destructive overwrite path.
- Keep matrix domains read-only: creation/rename controls apply only to normal `Components/` folders/files, never `Matrices/`.

### 3. Make Condition data source-aware
**Modify:** `src/types/schema.ts`, `src/utils/conditionManager.ts`, `src/store/useTriggerStore.ts`

- Extend the condition loading result so it retains each table’s filename/path and its individual dictionary, alongside the merged registry used by the condition-physics engine.
- Preserve the current merged `conditions` registry for `requirement`, `impact`, `tag_team`, and `conflicts_with` resolution. This ensures every condition table remains part of the same global condition graph.
- Refactor `ConditionManager` to:
  - list condition JSON tables and load/save an individual selected table;
  - create an empty named condition table;
  - rename a condition table without altering its entries;
  - continue treating `conditions.json` as the default table for backward compatibility.
- Change single-condition creation from component pickers to write explicitly to the default `conditions.json`, avoiding ambiguity when no Conditions table context exists.

### 4. Add named Condition table navigation and editing
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx`

- Add a **TABLES** row above the existing condition-category filter tabs.
- Let the Manager select the active condition table; display and edit only that table’s entries in the grid.
- Add `+ Table` and rename control using the same safe manager operations as Components.
- Save only the active table’s working dictionary—never the global merged registry.
- Keep the existing semantic `Category` tabs (Subject, Pose, Environment, etc.) as filters within the selected table; they are distinct from table navigation.
- Add a visible table label/path beside the current storage hint, so the Manager always sees which JSON table will be edited.

### 5. Protect reference integrity during structural renames
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx`, `src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx`

- Table and category renames retain JSON contents and Hex IDs, so cross-references (`requirement`, `impact`, `tag_team`, `conflicts_with`) remain valid with no migration.
- Do not provide delete controls in this first pass. Deletion is destructive and must be designed separately with dependency awareness and explicit confirmation.

## Verification

1. Run `npm run build` inside `.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger`; require a zero-error Vite build.
2. Components:
   - create a category, create an empty table in it, add/save an option;
   - rename the table, then rename the category;
   - confirm the JSON contents persist and the UI remains selected on the renamed objects.
3. Conditions:
   - create a second named conditions table, add/save a condition there, and rename it;
   - reopen the default `conditions.json` table and verify it was not overwritten;
   - confirm both tables contribute to the store’s merged condition registry and selectors.
4. Select a condition from the secondary condition table in a component’s requirement/impact picker; save and reload; confirm selection and conflict/tag-team physics still resolve.
5. Attempt duplicate, empty, separator-containing, and Windows-reserved names; confirm they are rejected without filesystem mutation.
6. Confirm no management controls appear for Matrix domains.

# Plan: Create & Rename Tables (Component Files) in Categories

## Context
The Manager wants the ability to **create new tables inside the "CATEGORIES" bar and rename them at will**. Today the Components studio only allows editing entries *within* pre-seeded JSON files. There is no UI to add a brand-new component file (table) or rename an existing one, and no UI to create/rename the category folders themselves.

Current architecture:
- **Categories** = folders under `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Components/` (e.g. `_01_Subject`, `_03_Apeals`)
- **Tables** = JSON files inside those folders (e.g. `1_subjects.json`), each holding a `Record<HexId, ComponentEntry>`
- Backend `ComponentManager.createComponentFile(app, folderRelPath, fileName)` already exists but is **unreachable from the UI**
- Obsidian `app.vault.adapter` exposes `rename(oldPath, newPath)`, `mkdir`, `exists`, `write`, `list`

## Scope
1. **Create a new component file (table)** in the active category — prompt for a name, write an empty `{}` JSON, select it.
2. **Rename a component file (table)** — rename the JSON file on disk, keep entries intact, update selection.
3. **Create a new category (folder)** — prompt for a name, `mkdir` under `Components/`.
4. **Rename a category (folder)** — `adapter.rename()` the folder; all child files move with it; update the selected folder/file references.
5. **Conditions** — already creatable via "+ Condition" row and inline "Create" in the multi-select; no new table concept applies (single `conditions.json` registry). No change needed there.

## Files to Modify
- `src/utils/componentManager.ts` — add `createCategoryFolder`, `renameCategoryFolder`, `renameComponentFile` static methods.
- `src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx` — add UI affordances:
  - File pills bar: `+ New Table` button (creates file in active folder).
  - Active file pill: rename on double-click / edit icon (rename file on disk).
  - Category pills bar: `+ New Category` button and per-pill rename affordance.
- `src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx` — no change (conditions already fully editable).

## Implementation Details
- All disk writes go through `app.vault.adapter` (never direct fs).
- After any create/rename, call `reload()` from the store so the scanner re-reads the tree and pills stay in sync.
- Use `generateHexId`-free plain names for files/folders (user-facing names); JSON filenames get `.json` appended.
- Rename must guard against overwriting an existing target; show `window.alert` on conflict.
- Empty new file seeds `{}` so the table opens empty ready for `+ Row`.

## Verification
1. `npm run build` in `.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger` → 0 errors.
2. Manual: open Components tab → click `+ New Category`, name it → appears in category bar → click `+ New Table`, name it → opens empty table → add a row → save.
3. Rename a table via double-click → file renamed on disk, entries preserved, table still selected.
4. Rename a category → all child files move, pills update, no broken references.

# Plan: Mirrored Folder/File Hierarchies for Components and Conditions

## Context
The requirement is precisely a mirrored two-tier filesystem model in both workspaces:

```text
Hazard_Trigger_Data/
├─ Components/
│  └─ _01_Subject/                  ← Category bar item / subfolder
│     └─ 1_subjects.json            ← Files bar item / table
└─ Conditions/
   └─ _00_Core/                     ← Category bar item / subfolder
      └─ conditions.json            ← Files bar item / condition table
```

The **Categories** bar must have a `+` action to create and rename subfolders. The **Files** bar must have a `+` action to create and rename JSON files inside the active subfolder. This is required for both Components and Conditions. The two systems differ only in their entry metadata and runtime treatment:

- Component JSON tables contain `ComponentEntry` objects and participate in selection/random/prompt generation.
- Condition JSON tables contain `ConditionEntry` objects; their entries merge into the global condition physics graph for `requirement`, `impact`, `tag_team`, and `conflicts_with` resolution.

The legacy root file `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/conditions.json` will be moved automatically to `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/_00_Core/conditions.json`, as explicitly chosen by the Manager.

## Recommended Implementation

### 1. Shared safe hierarchy management primitives
**Modify:** `src/utils/componentManager.ts`; create a parallel `src/utils/conditionManager.ts` API.

- Add strict safe-name validation for category folder and table filename creation/rename: non-empty trimmed names; reject separators, Windows-invalid characters/control characters, trailing dots/spaces, reserved device names, and collisions.
- Component operations:
  - `createCategoryFolder()` / `renameCategoryFolder()` for folders under `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Components/`.
  - keep `createComponentFile()` as the table creator, improving collision reporting.
  - `renameComponentFile()` to rename a JSON table while preserving its raw dictionary.
- Condition operations mirror Components exactly:
  - `createConditionCategoryFolder()`, `renameConditionCategoryFolder()`;
  - `createConditionFile()`, `renameConditionFile()`;
  - source-aware `saveConditionFile()` for one selected table.
- Use only Obsidian `app.vault.adapter` APIs (`exists`, `mkdir`, `write`, `read`, `rename`) and return the newly-created/renamed relative path so the UI can reselect it after `reload()`.

### 2. Component manager category/file controls
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx`

- Add a `+ Category` button at the end of the first **Categories** pill row.
- Add rename affordance for the selected normal Components category (not a Matrix domain).
- Add a `+ File` button at the end of the active category’s **Files** pill row.
- Add rename affordance for the selected file.
- Use prefilled native prompts and `window.alert` errors to match existing lightweight UI interactions.
- After each operation, `await reload()`, then set `selectedFolderId` / `selectedFileRelPath` to returned relative paths; reset the working copy through existing effects.
- Matrix domains remain read-only because they use a separate `Matrices/` schema and `_matrix.json` state definitions.

### 3. Promote Conditions to the same folder/file scanner model
**Modify:** `src/types/schema.ts`, `src/utils/conditionManager.ts`, `src/store/useTriggerStore.ts`

- Add `ConditionFileNode` and `ConditionFolderNode` types parallel to `ComponentFileNode` / `ComponentFolderNode`. Each condition file node holds its `relPath`, display name, and isolated `Record<string, ConditionEntry>`.
- Replace direct-file-only condition discovery with a one-level folder/file scan of `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/`, filtering to JSON tables and ignoring metadata/system files beginning with `_` only when they are JSON metadata files rather than folder names.
- Add a one-time migration in `ConditionManager.ensureConditionsFolder()`:
  1. create `_00_Core` if absent;
  2. if root `Conditions/conditions.json` exists and `_00_Core/conditions.json` does not, rename it into `_00_Core/conditions.json`;
  3. never overwrite an already-migrated target.
- Preserve a merged condition dictionary for `calculateState()` in the Zustand store, but retain the scanned folder/file tree separately for editing/navigation. Collision detection stays global across every condition table.
- Resolve duplicate Hex IDs deterministically (later sorted file loses or emits a console warning); new IDs are generated globally and practically collision-free.

### 4. Condition manager category/file controls and table-scoped editing
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx`

- Add the same two navigation rows used by Components:
  - **Categories:** condition subfolders plus `+ Category` and selected-folder rename.
  - **Files:** JSON condition tables in the selected folder plus `+ File` and selected-file rename.
- Replace its local `loadAllConditions()` editor source with the selected `ConditionFileNode.entries` dictionary.
- Keep the current semantic category filter tabs (*Subject*, *Pose*, *Environment*, etc.) beneath these navigation rows; they filter rows inside the active condition table and are not filesystem categories.
- Save/discard affects only the selected JSON file. After save or structural operations, refresh the Zustand store so global component selectors and collision physics see all condition tables.
- Update visible storage labels to show the active relative table path.

### 5. Retain global selector and physics semantics
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx`, `src/app/components/OptionEditorModal.tsx`, `src/store/useTriggerStore.ts`

- `NotionConditionMultiSelect` continues consuming the store’s globally merged `conditions` registry, so a component in any Components file can select a condition from any Conditions folder/file.
- Inline new-condition creation should save to the selected active condition file when that UI context is available; otherwise it falls back to `_00_Core/conditions.json`.
- Existing `requirement`, `impact`, `tag_team`, and `conflicts_with` continue to hold Hex IDs, so moving or renaming folders/files preserves all references without migration.

## Verification

1. Run `npm run build` in `.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger` and require a zero-error Vite build.
2. On initialization, verify legacy `Conditions/conditions.json` moves once to `Conditions/_00_Core/conditions.json` without data loss.
3. Components: create a category; create a JSON file in it; add and save an option; rename the file and folder; verify entries remain intact and selection follows the renamed paths.
4. Conditions: create a category and JSON file; add/save a condition; rename the file and folder; verify only the selected table changes while other condition tables remain unchanged.
5. Add a component requirement/impact pointing to a condition in a secondary Conditions table; reload; confirm condition selector, tag-team expansion, and conflict detection still function.
6. Attempt blank, duplicate, path-containing, and Windows-reserved names; confirm every attempt is rejected without any disk mutation.
7. Confirm Matrix domain folders/files do not display category/file creation or rename controls.

# Plan: Named Component & Condition Tables

## Context
The Manager wants the ability to create and rename named **tables** from the top-level **CATEGORIES** navigation—across both Components and Conditions.

The plugin currently treats Components as a two-level hierarchy:
- **Category**: a folder below `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Components/`.
- **Table**: a JSON file inside that folder, whose entries are `Record<HexId, ComponentEntry>`.

Conditions already live as JSON dictionaries below `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/`, but the manager currently merges *all* condition files for reading and always writes the aggregate dictionary back to `conditions.json`. That is incompatible with user-managed, independent condition tables: editing one table could collapse entries from every table into the default file. The work must therefore add source-aware condition-table loading/saving before its UI gains table creation and rename capabilities.

## Recommended Approach

### 1. Establish safe, reusable table/category file operations
**Modify:** `src/utils/componentManager.ts`

- Add one shared name normalizer/validator for user-created folder and file names:
  - trim whitespace;
  - reject empty names, path separators, Windows-invalid characters, control characters, reserved Windows device names, and names ending in `.` or spaces;
  - append `.json` only to component/condition table filenames;
  - reject collisions instead of silently overwriting.
- Add component hierarchy operations using Obsidian’s `app.vault.adapter`:
  - `createCategoryFolder()` creates `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Components/<category>/`.
  - `renameCategoryFolder()` atomically renames that folder, retaining all child tables and data.
  - reuse/upgrade `createComponentFile()` to create an empty `{}` table in the selected category.
  - `renameComponentFile()` renames an existing component JSON table while retaining its entries.
- Return the new vault-relative path on successful creation/rename, so the UI can explicitly reselect its item after reload.

### 2. Give Components category/table navigation full management controls
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx`

- Add `+ Category` to the top **CATEGORIES** row and `+ Table` to the selected category’s **FILES** row.
- Add an edit/rename action to the selected category and selected table pill; use pre-populated native prompts to match current lightweight in-app editing patterns.
- On success: call store `reload()`, update `selectedFolderId` / `selectedFileRelPath` to the returned path, and let the current working-copy synchronization initialize the new/renamed table.
- Surface validation, collision, and adapter failure messages with `window.alert`; no destructive overwrite path.
- Keep matrix domains read-only: creation/rename controls apply only to normal `Components/` folders/files, never `Matrices/`.

### 3. Make Condition data source-aware
**Modify:** `src/types/schema.ts`, `src/utils/conditionManager.ts`, `src/store/useTriggerStore.ts`

- Extend the condition loading result so it retains each table’s filename/path and its individual dictionary, alongside the merged registry used by the condition-physics engine.
- Preserve the current merged `conditions` registry for `requirement`, `impact`, `tag_team`, and `conflicts_with` resolution. This ensures every condition table remains part of the same global condition graph.
- Refactor `ConditionManager` to:
  - list condition JSON tables and load/save an individual selected table;
  - create an empty named condition table;
  - rename a condition table without altering its entries;
  - continue treating `conditions.json` as the default table for backward compatibility.
- Change single-condition creation from component pickers to write explicitly to the default `conditions.json`, avoiding ambiguity when no Conditions table context exists.

### 4. Add named Condition table navigation and editing
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx`

- Add a **TABLES** row above the existing condition-category filter tabs.
- Let the Manager select the active condition table; display and edit only that table’s entries in the grid.
- Add `+ Table` and rename control using the same safe manager operations as Components.
- Save only the active table’s working dictionary—never the global merged registry.
- Keep the existing semantic `Category` tabs (Subject, Pose, Environment, etc.) as filters within the selected table; they are distinct from table navigation.
- Add a visible table label/path beside the current storage hint, so the Manager always sees which JSON table will be edited.

### 5. Protect reference integrity during structural renames
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx`, `src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx`

- Table and category renames retain JSON contents and Hex IDs, so cross-references (`requirement`, `impact`, `tag_team`, `conflicts_with`) remain valid with no migration.
- Do not provide delete controls in this first pass. Deletion is destructive and must be designed separately with dependency awareness and explicit confirmation.

## Verification

1. Run `npm run build` inside `.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger`; require a zero-error Vite build.
2. Components:
   - create a category, create an empty table in it, add/save an option;
   - rename the table, then rename the category;
   - confirm the JSON contents persist and the UI remains selected on the renamed objects.
3. Conditions:
   - create a second named conditions table, add/save a condition there, and rename it;
   - reopen the default `conditions.json` table and verify it was not overwritten;
   - confirm both tables contribute to the store’s merged condition registry and selectors.
4. Select a condition from the secondary condition table in a component’s requirement/impact picker; save and reload; confirm selection and conflict/tag-team physics still resolve.
5. Attempt duplicate, empty, separator-containing, and Windows-reserved names; confirm they are rejected without filesystem mutation.
6. Confirm no management controls appear for Matrix domains.

# Plan: Mirrored Folder/File Hierarchies for Components and Conditions

## Context
The requirement is precisely a mirrored two-tier filesystem model in both workspaces:

```text
Hazard_Trigger_Data/
├─ Components/
│  └─ _01_Subject/                  ← Category bar item / subfolder
│     └─ 1_subjects.json            ← Files bar item / table
└─ Conditions/
   └─ _00_Core/                     ← Category bar item / subfolder
      └─ conditions.json            ← Files bar item / condition table
```

The **Categories** bar must have a `+` action to create and rename subfolders. The **Files** bar must have a `+` action to create and rename JSON files inside the active subfolder. This is required for both Components and Conditions. The two systems differ only in their entry metadata and runtime treatment:

- Component JSON tables contain `ComponentEntry` objects and participate in selection/random/prompt generation.
- Condition JSON tables contain `ConditionEntry` objects; their entries merge into the global condition physics graph for `requirement`, `impact`, `tag_team`, and `conflicts_with` resolution.

The legacy root file `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/conditions.json` will be moved automatically to `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/_00_Core/conditions.json`, as explicitly chosen by the Manager.

## Recommended Implementation

### 1. Shared safe hierarchy management primitives
**Modify:** `src/utils/componentManager.ts`; create a parallel `src/utils/conditionManager.ts` API.

- Add strict safe-name validation for category folder and table filename creation/rename: non-empty trimmed names; reject separators, Windows-invalid characters/control characters, trailing dots/spaces, reserved device names, and collisions.
- Component operations:
  - `createCategoryFolder()` / `renameCategoryFolder()` for folders under `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Components/`.
  - keep `createComponentFile()` as the table creator, improving collision reporting.
  - `renameComponentFile()` to rename a JSON table while preserving its raw dictionary.
- Condition operations mirror Components exactly:
  - `createConditionCategoryFolder()`, `renameConditionCategoryFolder()`;
  - `createConditionFile()`, `renameConditionFile()`;
  - source-aware `saveConditionFile()` for one selected table.
- Use only Obsidian `app.vault.adapter` APIs (`exists`, `mkdir`, `write`, `read`, `rename`) and return the newly-created/renamed relative path so the UI can reselect it after `reload()`.

### 2. Component manager category/file controls
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx`

- Add a `+ Category` button at the end of the first **Categories** pill row.
- Add rename affordance for the selected normal Components category (not a Matrix domain).
- Add a `+ File` button at the end of the active category’s **Files** pill row.
- Add rename affordance for the selected file.
- Use prefilled native prompts and `window.alert` errors to match existing lightweight UI interactions.
- After each operation, `await reload()`, then set `selectedFolderId` / `selectedFileRelPath` to returned relative paths; reset the working copy through existing effects.
- Matrix domains remain read-only because they use a separate `Matrices/` schema and `_matrix.json` state definitions.

### 3. Promote Conditions to the same folder/file scanner model
**Modify:** `src/types/schema.ts`, `src/utils/conditionManager.ts`, `src/store/useTriggerStore.ts`

- Add `ConditionFileNode` and `ConditionFolderNode` types parallel to `ComponentFileNode` / `ComponentFolderNode`. Each condition file node holds its `relPath`, display name, and isolated `Record<string, ConditionEntry>`.
- Replace direct-file-only condition discovery with a one-level folder/file scan of `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/`, filtering to JSON tables and ignoring metadata/system files beginning with `_` only when they are JSON metadata files rather than folder names.
- Add a one-time migration in `ConditionManager.ensureConditionsFolder()`:
  1. create `_00_Core` if absent;
  2. if root `Conditions/conditions.json` exists and `_00_Core/conditions.json` does not, rename it into `_00_Core/conditions.json`;
  3. never overwrite an already-migrated target.
- Preserve a merged condition dictionary for `calculateState()` in the Zustand store, but retain the scanned folder/file tree separately for editing/navigation. Collision detection stays global across every condition table.
- Resolve duplicate Hex IDs deterministically (later sorted file loses or emits a console warning); new IDs are generated globally and practically collision-free.

### 4. Condition manager category/file controls and table-scoped editing
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx`

- Add the same two navigation rows used by Components:
  - **Categories:** condition subfolders plus `+ Category` and selected-folder rename.
  - **Files:** JSON condition tables in the selected folder plus `+ File` and selected-file rename.
- Replace its local `loadAllConditions()` editor source with the selected `ConditionFileNode.entries` dictionary.
- Keep the current semantic category filter tabs (*Subject*, *Pose*, *Environment*, etc.) beneath these navigation rows; they filter rows inside the active condition table and are not filesystem categories.
- Save/discard affects only the selected JSON file. After save or structural operations, refresh the Zustand store so global component selectors and collision physics see all condition tables.
- Update visible storage labels to show the active relative table path.

### 5. Retain global selector and physics semantics
**Modify:** `src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx`, `src/app/components/OptionEditorModal.tsx`, `src/store/useTriggerStore.ts`

- `NotionConditionMultiSelect` continues consuming the store’s globally merged `conditions` registry, so a component in any Components file can select a condition from any Conditions folder/file.
- Inline new-condition creation should save to the selected active condition file when that UI context is available; otherwise it falls back to `_00_Core/conditions.json`.
- Existing `requirement`, `impact`, `tag_team`, and `conflicts_with` continue to hold Hex IDs, so moving or renaming folders/files preserves all references without migration.

## Verification

1. Run `npm run build` in `.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger` and require a zero-error Vite build.
2. On initialization, verify legacy `Conditions/conditions.json` moves once to `Conditions/_00_Core/conditions.json` without data loss.
3. Components: create a category; create a JSON file in it; add and save an option; rename the file and folder; verify entries remain intact and selection follows the renamed paths.
4. Conditions: create a category and JSON file; add/save a condition; rename the file and folder; verify only the selected table changes while other condition tables remain unchanged.
5. Add a component requirement/impact pointing to a condition in a secondary Conditions table; reload; confirm condition selector, tag-team expansion, and conflict detection still function.
6. Attempt blank, duplicate, path-containing, and Windows-reserved names; confirm every attempt is rejected without any disk mutation.
7. Confirm Matrix domain folders/files do not display category/file creation or rename controls.

The mirrored two-tier hierarchy is now implemented and active across both **Components** and **Conditions**, Manager.

---

### Key Architectural Updates

1. **Exact Mirrored Filesystem Model**:
   ```text
   Hazard_Trigger_Data/
   ├── Components/
   │   └── <Category_Folder>/
   │       └── <Table_Name>.json
   └── Conditions/
       └── <Category_Folder>/
           └── <Table_Name>.json
   ```

2. **Autonomous Legacy Migration**:
   - [ConditionManager.ensureConditionsFolder()](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/utils/conditionManager.ts#L48) checks for root `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/conditions.json` and moves it safely into `Hazard_Trigger_Data/Conditions/_00_Core/conditions.json` without data loss.

3. **`+ Category` & `+ File` Navigation Bars**:
   - **Components Tab** ([ComponentsManagerView.tsx](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx#L510)):
     - **Categories Bar**: Displays component subfolders + `+ Category` button + Rename `✎` button for the active category.
     - **Files Bar**: Displays JSON tables inside the selected category + `+ File` button + Rename `✎` button for the active table.
   - **Conditions Tab** ([ConditionsManagerView.tsx](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx#L485)):
     - **Categories Bar**: Displays condition subfolders + `+ Category` button + Rename `✎` button.
     - **Files Bar**: Displays condition JSON tables in the active subfolder + `+ File` button + Rename `✎` button.
     - **Filter Tags Bar**: Retains semantic tags (*Subject*, *Pose*, *Apparel*, etc.) to filter rows **within** the selected table.

4. **Global Reference & Physics Integrity**:
   - Condition tables are saved individually to their source files (e.g. `Conditions/_00_Core/conditions.json`).
   - The scanner merges all conditions across all folders into the global runtime physics graph, ensuring component `requirement`, `impact`, `tag_team`, and `conflicts_with` lookups continue resolving seamlessly across tables.

5. **Production Verification**:

Both errors have been diagnosed and resolved, Manager:

---

### Root Causes & Fixes Applied

1. **Fixed `EPERM: operation not permitted, rename 'conditions.json' -> '_00_Core\conditions.json'`**:
   - **Root Cause**: In Windows / Google Drive virtual file systems, `adapter.rename` threw an `EPERM` lock error when attempting to move the root file across directories.
   - **Fix**: Updated [ConditionManager.ensureConditionsFolder()](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/utils/conditionManager.ts#L48) to perform a non-blocking read-and-write copy migration with soft deletion, wrapped in try/catch so file locks never crash `TriggerStore.init()`.

2. **Fixed `Uncaught (in promise) Error: prompt() is not supported.`**:
   - **Root Cause**: Obsidian runs on Electron where the native browser `window.prompt()` API is explicitly blocked by the Chromium renderer.
   - **Fix**: Created a dedicated React component [HierarchyPromptModal.tsx](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/app/components/HierarchyPromptModal.tsx).
   - Wired the modal into both [ComponentsManagerView.tsx](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/app/components/ComponentsManagerView.tsx) and [ConditionsManagerView.tsx](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx) with:

The clumsy native dropdowns have been replaced with full Notion-style searchable multi-select selectors, Manager:

---

### What Was Built & Replaced

1. **New `NotionTagTeamMultiSelect` Component** ([NotionTagTeamMultiSelect.tsx](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/app/components/NotionTagTeamMultiSelect.tsx)):
   - **Live Type-To-Search Input**: Auto-focuses immediately upon opening. Filters across:
     - Component Display Name
     - Hex Key ID
     - Source Category / Subfolder
     - Source File Table
     - Raw Prompt Tokens
   - **Category & Folder Filter Tabs**: Quickly isolate options by specific component domains (e.g., *Subject*, *Apparel*, *Pose*).
   - **Rich Option Preview Cards**: Displays Option Name, File origin badge, and prompt token snippets.
   - **Seamless Multi-Select**: Checkbox toggle on click, instant pill removal with <kbd>X</kbd>, and no cell overflow.

2. **New `NotionConditionRelationSelect` Component** ([NotionConditionRelationSelect.tsx](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/app/components/NotionConditionRelationSelect.tsx)):
   - Replaced both the raw `+ Bundle...` (Tag-Team) and `+ Conflict...` (Collision) native selects in [ConditionsManagerView.tsx](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/app/components/ConditionsManagerView.tsx#L960).
   - Search across all condition names, Hex IDs, categories, and descriptions with instant type-ahead filtering.

3. **Production Verified**:
   - Recompiled cleanly with **0 errors**. Reload Obsidian (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd>) to try the new searchable Tag-Team and Inheritance selectors.

The transitive tag-team inheritance architecture is fully implemented and compiled, Manager.

---

### What Was Built

1. **New `resolveTagTeamLineage()` Function** ([useTriggerStore.ts](.obsidian/plugins/obsidian-hazard-trigger/src/store/useTriggerStore.ts#L195)):
   - Recursively walks the full `tag_team` inheritance chain (e.g. `lying on back` → `lying` → `resting`).
   - **Merges in base-to-derived order**, so the most specific entry always wins for:
     - **Requirements** (preconditions needed)
     - **Impacts / Keywords** (state assertions)
     - **Exclusions / Anti-prompt** (subtractions)
     - **Prompt tokens** (prepended building blocks)
     - **Subject vector** (most specific takes effect)
   - Returns a clean payload with deduplicated, exclusion-filtered token lists.

2. **Automatic Propagation in Both Passes**:
   - **Pass 1 (Fixed Selections)**: Every explicitly selected component now resolves its full lineage and injects inherited `requirement`, `impact`, `keywords`, and `anti-prompt` into the global active keyword/exclusion sets.
   - **Pass 2 (Random Selections)**: Randomly rolled components do the same, so even gacha-selected items inherit their base blocks' condition physics.

3. **Prompt Compilation Integration**:
   - Inherited `combinedPromptTokens` are prepended to the derived component's own prompt during the folder-block compilation phase.
   - Anti-prompt deduplication works across both inherited and local tokens.

4. **Condition Physics Inheritance**:
   - If base component `"lying"` requires `"condition_horizontal"` and asserts `"condition_prone"`, then `"lying on back"` (which `tag_team`s `"lying"`) **automatically** gets both without needing to re-pick them.
   - Collision detection and tag-team expansion on the Condition side continue to operate on the full expanded set.

5. **Production Verified**:
   - Clean Vite build with **0 errors**. Reload Obsidian (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd>) to test the inheritance chain.

---

### Manager Workflow

1. Define **base block** (e.g. `"lying"`) with its `requirement` + `impact` once.
2. Create **derived component** (e.g. `"lying on back"`) and add `tag_team: ["lying"]`.
3. That's it—requirements, impacts, and prompt fragments from `"lying"` flow into `"lying on back"` automatically. No repetition.

# Plan: Reverse Engineering Tab - Set-Difference Workflow Rebuild

## Context
The Manager wants to rebuild the Reverse Engineering tab with a clear **set-difference workflow**:
1. Text area → paste "wild completed prompt" → `split(',')` + `strip()` → `wild_prompt_set`
2. Load all existing component prompts → `components_set`
3. Compute `filtered_set = wild_prompt_set - components_set` (set difference)
4. Convert `filtered_set` back to a regular prompt string

This replaces the current token-by-token decompiler with a cleaner set-based approach.

## Current Architecture
- `promptDecompiler.ts` - Token-level decompiler with fuzzy matching (exact/strong/partial/keyword)
- `ReverseEngineeringView.tsx` - UI with matched sections grid, token map, unmatched tokens
- Uses `sanitizeToken()`, `extractRawTokens()` from `promptDecompiler.ts`

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Update `promptDecompiler.ts` - Core Set-Difference Logic
**New function: `decomposePromptWithSetDifference(prompt, folders, matrixDomains)`**
- Accepts raw prompt string and component libraries
- Returns structured result with:
  - `wildPromptSet: string[]` - All stripped tokens from input
  - `componentsSet: Map<string, string[]>` - Per-component-file token sets (key = relPath, value = token array)
  - `matchedTokens: string[]` - Intersection (wild ∩ components)
  - `unmatchedTokens: string[]` - Difference (wild - components)  
  - `matchedComponents: Array<{relPath, matchedTokens, entry}>` - Which components matched what
  - `reconstructedPrompt: string` - Unmatched tokens rejoined with commas

**Reuse existing utilities:**
- `sanitizeToken()` - Strip weights, parens, normalize
- `extractRawTokens()` - Split on comma/newline/BREAK

### 2. Rewrite `ReverseEngineeringView.tsx` - New UI
**Three-panel layout:**

**Panel A: Wild Prompt Input**
- Textarea (expandable) + Paste/Load Studio buttons
- Live token count display
- "Components Database" stats badge (total components, total tokens)

**Panel B: Matched Components Breakdown**
- List of component files that contributed tokens
- For each: file name, display name, count of matched tokens, confidence
- Toggle to show/hide matched tokens per component
- "Adopt to Studio" button per component (sets selection)

**Panel C: Residual / Unmatched Tokens (The Difference)**
- Clean token cloud of `filtered_set = wild - components`
- "Copy Residual Prompt" button (ready for new component creation)
- "Create New Component from Residual" button (opens OptionEditorModal with prefilled prompt)

### 3. Component Prompt Extraction
**New helper: `getAllComponentPromptTokens(folders, matrixDomains)`**
- Returns `Map<string, {tokens: string[], entry: ComponentEntry, file: ComponentFileNode}>`
- Key = file relPath
- Pre-processes all component prompts into deduplicated token sets
- Includes matrix domain base state prompts

### 4. Set Difference Algorithm
```
wildTokens = extractRawTokens(prompt).map(sanitizeToken).map(t => t.clean)
```
